1-4 = Firm. 72r a. 1 praecedentibus bonis meliora decernit, Firm. 3 εὔχαρι

sections.en:
1-4 = Firm. 72r a. 1 decrees better things than the preceding good things, Firm. 3 εὔχαρι ('charming')
M, I have corrected with hesitation; cf. Firm., both the marks of a distinguished art and the order of an honorable conversa-
tion and the grace of sweet speech. 5-9 = Firm. 74v a. 11-20 from Valens
above p. 91, 12. 13 φωσασκίας ('of light-exercise') M. 17 νομικούς ('lawyers') that is, legal consultants. 20-25 from
Ptol. 43r, 18-24 from which he took ἐναντίαν διάθεσιν ('opposite disposition'), although concerning ἐνδόξῳ ('glorious')
he said nothing. 21 εὐστίχους ('well-lined') M. 26-28 he transcribed as it seems from Ptol. 41v, 16-20 contrary to
custom; the following things again are said concerning Mercury alone. 28 ἀθεμετουργίας ('of lawless deeds') M.
29-34 from Ptol. 22v, 22 - 31 (where l. 22, write δυσπλοίας ('of bad sailing')). 30 τῶν ἱερατικῶν ('of the priestly things') M. 31 ἐθέ-
μων ('of customs') M. 34 sq. = Ptol. 38v, 2.

summary.headline: Mercury and Venus Configurations
summary.text: Astrological delineations of Venus decanating or diametrizing the Moon, including effects on marriage, jealousy, childlessness, and women. A section on Mercury lists his domains, professions, mental qualities, vices when afflicted or configured with Saturn, and effects on religion, laws, winds, thunder, lightning, chasms, and earthquakes.
